=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs`, `--limit 100` | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The single `gh run list --event workflow_dispatch --limit 100` call returns at most 100 runs. A repo with more than 100 workflow_dispatch runs could have the PR-named run aged out of the first page of results; the function then returns `[]`, and the caller (active-run guard, failed-autofix redispatch, or direct-inflight fallback) proceeds as if no named run exists.
  WHY: A duplicate review dispatch against a PR that already has a live dispatch run named for it. The per-cycle dispatch tracker and concurrency group bound the damage to one extra run, and the function's fail-open contract is documented. In practice this requires over 100 workflow_dispatch runs between the dispatched run and the poller's next lookup.
  severity=NIT; ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` (lines 17370-17429)
  PROBLEM: `--limit 100` is a hard cap. If a repo has >100 `workflow_dispatch` runs since a PR's last review, the newest PR-named run could fall off the listing. The retrigger failed-autofix check (lines 13775-13807) and the `_direct_inflight_review_run_on_branch` fallback (lines 12621-12644) would then return empty and either push an empty commit or skip a legitimate in-flight detection. Today's per-PR cadence keeps this rare, but the same lookup is shared by three callers, all of which assume it covers the most recent activity.
  WHY: Suggested minimal fix: when no PR-named run is found and the oldest `createdAt` in the returned page is younger than `PR_NAMED_LOOKUP_MAX_AGE_HOURS` (default 24), fetch one more page (`gh run list --event workflow_dispatch --limit 100` with the next page token) before failing open to `[]`. Falls back to the current behavior whenever the page already covers the window. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
- scripts/review_merge_train.sh, `_mt_release` at line 461
  PROBLEM: `printf '%s\n' "${inflight_review_branches}" | grep -Fxq -e "${head}" -e "pr:${num}"` matches an empty `${head}` against every blank line in the listing. A `--branch`-filtered raw REST listing can include runs with `head_branch: null` (workflow_dispatch runs whose `head_branch` is empty on the API), and a `pr:<N>` run with a missing branch label would be indistinguishable from a `head=""` PR. PRs without a head branch are rare but valid for comment-only edits, and the current grep would treat any blank line in the listing as a hit.
  WHY: Suggested minimal fix: guard the head match with `[ -n "${head}" ]` before the grep, or feed `printf '%s\n' "pr:${num}"` only when `head` is empty. A 2-line change preserves the existing `pr:<N>` semantics. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh, `_direct_inflight_review_run_on_branch` at line 12621
  PROBLEM: The PR-named jq filter (`[ .[]? | select((.status // "") == "in_progress" or (.status // "") == "queued" or (.status // "") == "pending") | ... ]`) parses `startedAt` then `createdAt` to derive a start epoch, but if both are missing it falls back to `$now` (`if $ts != "" then ... else $now end`). A future-dated run with neither field would be treated as `now`, which always passes the freshness filter (`($now - $start_epoch) < $threshold`). Today this is only an issue if `startedAt`/`createdAt` are both empty (rare), but the same pattern is copied in `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs`'s callers, so a regression propagates.
  WHY: Suggested minimal fix: treat a missing timestamp as already-stale by defaulting `$start_epoch` to `0` (so the freshness check fails) instead of `$now`. One-line change. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
